advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an attested-gate-config test asserting a no-verified_at_sha (pre-S4b/local-signed) attestation with an UNCHANGED committed dependency certifies via the current-gate-ref basis (the documented 'legacy tolerance' contract).
evidence: manifest.py:215-216: 'Legacy tolerance: an attestation with no ``verified_at_sha`` (pre-S4b) still verifies — its signed hashes are simply compared against the same current-gate-ref basis.'
search 'verified_at_sha' in attest.py returned no matches — claim_gate_check no longer reads the pin, so a no-pin attestation flows through at_current_gate_ref=True under attested config

test_ref_coherence.py:138 `monkeypatch.setenv("REBAR_GATE_SOURCE", "local")` — the only no-pin coherence test uses local, which degrades to the working tree and never exercises the attested current-gate-ref path against a no-pin manifest

test_opcert_local_verify_binding.py:311 `good_hash = _hash_file("watched.py", base=_hash_basis(repo_root=str(store)))` computes the manifest hash from the working-tree basis, not the current-gate-ref snapshot the gate later uses
advisory.finding: The newly documented 'Legacy tolerance' contract — a pre-S4b attestation carrying no verified_at_sha still VERIFIES with its signed hashes compared against the current-gate-ref basis (manifest.py:215-216; attest.py no longer reads verified_at_sha at all) — has no end-to-end test in ATTESTED gate config for the certified (unchanged-dependency) direction. The only no-pin coherence test (test_local_gate_config_uses_working_tree_basis_on_both_sides) sets source=local, which short-circuits to the working tree before reaching the current-gate-ref path; the opcert unit tests build good_hash from the working-tree basis (_hash_basis without at_current_gate_ref) and pass only because tree==HEAD, so they do not independently prove the attested current-gate-ref basis certifies a no-pin manifest.
scenarios: A pre-S4b / local-signed attestation is claim-checked in a repo whose gate config is attested (the production default) and the reviewed dependency is UNCHANGED — the documented contract says this must certify.
